newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks hit new highs, Tokyo slips.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks hit new highs, Tokyo slips.

text.p: Hong Kong shares continued their record-shattering run on Wednesday, hitting another all-time high and record close.
But Tokyo stocks slipped as investors took profits on the market's three-day upswing.
Asia's markets closed generally mixed, after Wall Street's moderate losses last night failed to provide inspiration.
Domestic issues dominated most of the region's markets.

Bombay shares shed 2.11 percent after a see-saw session, with auto and cement stocks leading the slide. Seoul's main index, however, advanced 0.93 percent on bargain-hunting. Brokers said Hong Kong's Hang Seng index shrugged off early weakness on futures-related activity and buying in favoured property developers.
The Hang Seng Index rose 45.62 points or 0.34 percent, to end at 13,530.95, its highest level ever, topping the previous record of 13,495.38 set on Tuesday afternoon.

"We saw the start of a correction in the morning, but futures-related buying in the last hour of afternoon trading pushed the index up," said Jason Tang, from institutional sales at South China Securities.
Tokyo's key Nikkei 225 index ended on a feeble note, down 72.97 points or 0.34 percent at 21,345.28.
Brokers blamed profit-taking, after the index rose for three straight sessions. The impact of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" business sentiment survey released in the morning was limited, they added.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index sank 64.87 points to end at 2,883.57 after a volatile session. Selling of auto and cement stocks dragged the main index lower, brokers said.
"Short covering at the end pulled prices slightly higher but there was a conspicuous absence of buyers during the day," said a chief dealer at a foreign brokerage.
"Large investors don't feel good about this market."
Jakarta shares were also dented by profit-taking. The composite index fell 5.96 points, or 0.95 percent, to end at 620.27 points.
Brokers said further profit-taking was likely on Thursday.
Seoul stocks finished in positive territory, boosted by bargain hunting after recent sharp falls, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 6.65 points to a provisional close of 722.62.

Taiwan's key index failed to challenge the 7,000-point resistance level. The weighted index closed 5.19 points or a scant 0.07 percent higher at 6,932.96, after waves of profit- taking eroded early gains.
Thai stocks were hemmed in a narrow range all day, trapped by market concerns about the Thai economic slowdown and the shape of a new Thai cabinet, brokers said.
The SET index rose 1.09 points to 959.23 at the finish on thin turnover.
Singapore shares ended little changed but dealers said the market's trend remained positive. The key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) crept up 0.48 point to 2,220.36 at the close.
"Profit taking will alternate with spells of buying," said one dealer.
Sydney's All Ordinaries index lost 5.3 points to close at 2,376.7.
But the market was helped off its session lows by bargain-hunting ahead of the close, traders said.
Brent crude futures finished firmer, buoyed by gains in NYMEX crudes on bullish overnight U.S. stock data.
January Brent crude futures were last traded on SIMEX at $22.90 per barrel, up 16 cents from London's settlement.
The dollar was slightly stronger in sluggish trading, amid a lack of fresh factors.
At 1150 GMT the dollar traded at 113.21/26 yen and 1.5238/48 marks.
